prompt: Write the clause that keeps only groups whose total lag is above zero. This test is on an aggregate, so it must come after GROUP BY and use HAVING with SUM(p.log_end_offset - c.committed_offset) > 0.
given: Query: SELECT c.group_id, SUM(...) AS total_lag FROM ... GROUP BY c.group_id <your clause> ORDER BY ...
template:
-- EXPECTED: [["billing", 60], ["zeta", 60], ["fraud", 50], ["analytics", 40]]

-- Tables are loaded for you: partitions(topic, partition_id, log_end_offset) and commits(group_id, topic, partition_id, committed_offset).
SELECT c.group_id,
       SUM(p.log_end_offset - c.committed_offset) AS total_lag
FROM commits c
JOIN partitions p ON p.topic = c.topic AND p.partition_id = c.partition_id
GROUP BY c.group_id
@@BLANK@@
ORDER BY total_lag DESC, c.group_id ASC
;
why: HAVING filters after aggregation; WHERE cannot see SUM. Repeat the aggregate expression because aliases are not available here in all databases.
